newsitem.title: USA: Shopko bonds up, Phar-Mor falls as merger deal off.
newsitem.headline: Shopko bonds up, Phar-Mor falls as merger deal off.

text.p: Bonds of Shopko Stores Inc gained a few points on Wednesday following news that the company's merger with Phar-Mor Inc was called off, traders said.
"Movement in Shopko and Phar-Mor bonds provided some action in an otherwise quiet corporate market today," said one trader.
Shopko's 9-1/4 debt due 2022 was quoted up over three points higher to trade at a 103 bid, 104 offered, traders said.
The company's 8-1/2 percent paper due 2002 and 9.0 percent debt due 2004, also traded up a couple of points to trade at 104 bid and 101-1/2 offered, respectively.
Phar-Mor bonds traded off a couple of points to trade at a 98-1/2 bid, 100-1/2 offered, traders said.

Earlier, the companies said they had terminated by mutual agreement their planned $1.0 bilion merger, which was first announced in September 1996. The companies cited continuing uncertainties in consummating the transaction and said they would pursue their respective goals separately.
Shopko Stores' senior unecured debt is rated Baa2 by Moody's Investors Service Inc and BBB by Standard & Poor's.
Phar-Mor senior unsecured debt is rated B3 by Moody's and and B-minus by S&P.

Under the previously planned merger, drug retailer Phar-Mor would have merged with retailer Shopko, creating a new company to be called Cabot Noble Inc. Cabot would have had combined annual sales of about $3.2 billion and 232 stores in 29 states.
